analyst_view.overall: Bottom against top at the Alfonso Murube on Monday night: Ceuta are last with 5 points from 14 games, eight from safety, and lost 2-0 at Tenerife in Sergio Lobera's first game after José Juan Romero was sacked. Almería, under Xavier García Pimienta, lead with 32 points, are unbeaten in 11 and have the best defence (11 conceded), with Miguel de la Fuente the league's top scorer; a local analyst notes they have struggled to hold leads late in games over the past month. Lobera has had a full week to bring in his possession and pressing ideas; at Tenerife Ceuta had about 64% of the ball but few clear chances. Almería get Marcos Luna back from a ban and Dzodic and Cipenga back from international duty, with only Ely and Melamed out; Ceuta's Edgar Sevikyan went off injured at Tenerife with no update since. No referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, 1.2 of them Ceuta's, helped by last season's 3-2 home win in the head-to-head. I lean slightly lower, to about 3.1: Ceuta have scored 10 in 14 and under Lobera had the ball at Tenerife but little presence in the box, Sevikyan is a doubt, and Almería have conceded only 11 all season. Almería's own scoring is already in the numbers.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, 6.1 of them Ceuta's, which already includes their recent run of winning lots of corners (+11.4% momentum). Lobera's possession style fits that pattern rather than changing it, and Almería tend to let opponents have the ball, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards, already counting Ceuta's heavy recent booking (+12% momentum). Ceuta are desperate and at Tenerife were booked for stopping counters when their press was beaten, which is the same pattern; no referee has been named yet, so I stay at 6.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.3 shots, with Ceuta's recent shot volume already adding a large 30% to their side. Under Lobera they kept the ball and shot from range, while Almería tend to need few chances; that fits what the numbers already expect, so I stay at 31.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. In line with my goals lean I take a little off, to about 10.0: Ceuta managed only two on target at Tenerife despite most of the ball, their shooting is mostly from distance, and Sevikyan may be missing; Almería's own accuracy and their solid defence are already in the numbers.
